verdict.root_cause: Every PlaceOrder trace terminates at the same span: checkoutservice's call to CartService/GetCart errors in under a millisecond, and the ERROR status on prepareOrderItemsAndShippingQuoteFromCart, checkoutservice PlaceOrder, frontend PlaceOrder and frontend HTTP POST is inherited from that child [tr_cf78d6313604]. No payment, shipping, currency, catalog or email span is ever emitted, so checkout aborts before reaching any other dependency. Checkoutservice is alive, taking steady traffic, logs no errors, and its own error ratio fell versus baseline [tr_efdaef307712][tr_f41d8283becb]; frontend's error signal is bursty and indistinguishable from the prior hour, so the edge is reporting rather than originating [tr_e64738bc84db]. Blame sits on cartservice, which is hard-failing every GetCart. The mechanism inside cartservice is not established: no cartservice logs, metrics or change history were ever queried, and the two change queries that ran covered only checkoutservice and paymentservice with its one-hop neighbours, both empty [tr_5218f0eb5cea][tr_399edc9ea372].
verdict.reasoning: Localization is strong: the deepest erroring span in every sampled trace is CartService/GetCart, all ancestors inherit ERROR, and no downstream-of-cart spans exist, which excludes payment, shipping, currency and email as origins and excludes a hang, since all spans close in single-digit milliseconds [tr_cf78d6313604]. Checkoutservice is exonerated as origin by its healthy process and absent error logs [tr_efdaef307712], by its error ratio dropping to ~0.4x baseline with no sustained departure [tr_f41d8283becb], and by an empty 24-hour change log [tr_5218f0eb5cea]. Frontend is the alerting service, not the failing one [tr_e64738bc84db]. Paymentservice is cleared twice over: its metric selector is empty in both windows, a pre-existing instrumentation gap [tr_0e052aecec82], and its change history is empty [tr_399edc9ea372]. Because no dispatch ever observed cartservice directly, I will not name resource_exhaustion, bad_config or bad_deploy as settled — the fast-fail signature admits all three.
open_questions: cartservice was never dispatched to; the actual error GetCart returns (refused, OOM, auth, deadline) is unknown.
Is a cart backing store (redis/valkey) behind cartservice the real failure, rather than cartservice itself?
No change record was sought for cartservice or its backend, so a change-driven onset there remains untested.

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice's cache backend exhausted memory or connections, making every GetCart fail immediately.
alternatives.why_not: Plausible and consistent with a deterministic fast-fail, but no cartservice or backend metric was ever collected to show saturation.

alternatives.root_cause: A cartservice config value (backend address, port or credential) is wrong, so every cart lookup is rejected at connect time.
alternatives.why_not: No change history was queried for cartservice; the only change logs run were empty for other services, so there is no recorded edit to point at.

proposal.expected_effect: No action is proposed, so no change in any series is expected. The failure signature should persist unchanged: every PlaceOrder trace continuing to terminate at checkoutservice -> hipstershop.CartService/GetCart with ERROR in under 1ms, and checkoutservice logs continuing to show PlaceOrder request-start lines with no follow-on payment/email/publish lines. The next step is investigative, not remediative: query cartservice logs (loki, {service="cart-service"}), cartservice error-ratio and restart/uptime metrics, and change_history for cartservice with a one-hop radius so its backing store (redis/valkey) is covered. Those three results would either meet the preconditions of restart_service (process-state evidence: crash loop, OOM kill, connection-refused on the cart backend) or of rollback_image/revert_config (a recorded deploy or config change on cartservice or its store).
proposal.if_wrong: This abstention is wrong if the three pending queries come back showing an unambiguous process-state fault confined to cartservice - e.g. repeated startup banners, OOM/panic lines, or a rising restart counter - with an empty change history for cartservice and its store. In that case restart_service on cartservice becomes the correct proposal and the delay cost real orders. It is also wrong if cartservice turns out to emit no logs and no metrics at all, in which case the mechanism can never be observed from this system and a blind recreate is the only lever available; that case should be escalated to a human rather than resolved by this system.
proposal.risk: The risk of abstaining is continued total checkout failure: the trace sample contains no successful PlaceOrder, so the customer-facing outage persists for as long as the investigation takes. The risk of the alternative - proposing restart_service on cartservice now - is what drives this abstention: restart_service is marked irreversible, its stated precondition is that evidence points at process state, and there is zero evidence of any kind from cartservice. No cartservice logs, metrics or change history were ever queried [tr_5218f0eb5cea][tr_399edc9ea372], so the sub-millisecond GetCart error [tr_cf78d6313604] is equally consistent with a crashed process, an auth/config rejection, or a dead redis/valkey behind cartservice. If the backing store is the real fault, a recreate fixes nothing, destroys the in-process state and log tail that would have identified the mechanism, and burns the one irreversible action on a wrong target.
proposal.blast_radius: Nobody sees a change, because nothing changes. The parties already affected remain affected: frontend and loadgenerator on the PlaceOrder path, and every checkout caller downstream of it. Had restart_service been proposed against cartservice, the blast radius would have been cartservice's container plus its inbound callers - frontend (cart view, add-to-cart) and checkoutservice - which would see connection resets for the duration of the recreate, widening the outage from checkout-only to cart-and-checkout.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical severity across frontend and checkoutservice near-simultaneously, with loadgenerator also alerting, describes a user-facing failure that cannot be dismissed. No open incidents to attribute it to, and the alert pattern alone does not distinguish a bad deploy from a failing downstream dependency.
